items.title: Resident Evil's Zach Cregger Admits He Was 'Naive' to Assume Fans Would Approve of Him Avoiding a Direct Adaptation of the Games
items.description: Zach Cregger admitted that he was “naive” to think his less-direct approach to adapting Resident Evil would be universally well-received by fans after deliberately choosing to avoid retelling the story exactly as it unfolds in the games.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Zach Cregger admitted that he was “naive” to think his less-direct approach to adapting Resident Evil would be universally well-received by fans after deliberately choosing to avoid retelling the story exactly as it unfolds in the games.

Cregger’s Resident Evil movie follows Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who gets caught up in the madness of the Raccoon City Incident. The writer/director confirmed previously that this film takes place in parallel to the events of Resident Evil 2 and that it focuses more on what it feels like as a player to navigate through zombie-filled corridors and sneak around Lickers… but not everyone was anticipating an original story told within the continuity of Capcom’s beloved horror game franchise.

Instead, a slew of fans have lashed out at Cregger for not directly adapting an existing game in the series, with many arguing that, without characters like Leon, Ada, and Jill, this isn’t really a Resident Evil movie at all.

IGN’s Tom Jorgensen got the chance to sit down with Cregger to ask him about his feelings on this particular topic — and his response was strikingly self-aware.

“I think I was naive,” he said. “I thought fans of these games, like me, would be thrilled that somebody was coming along and turning Resident Evil into a survival horror movie. I was like, ‘That’s great.’ I did not really appreciate the sentiment that, ‘We’ve been waiting forever for Leon’s story.’ And I appreciate that, and I’m sorry that’s not the story I’m bringing. I get it, I understand the frustration. I understand it so well because I haven’t seen the earlier [Resident Evil] movies, because they don't look like the Resident Evil that I love, so how could I be frustrated with fans who have that same attitude?

“My only hope is that they’ll see the movie regardless of their skepticism or their disappointment that I’m not telling some of the stories that the games tell so well, and they will feel seen when they do watch the movie, and they will recognize all of the love for the games that are in this movie, because it is there. This is not me just telling a story and slapping Resident Evil on it so I can get a budget. This is me telling a Resident Evil story. I understand the resistance, I do, because I have it myself. It is coming from a true place of love.”

Cregger’s love for the Resident Evil series is evident in multiple references that have been included in his movie, a few of which fans have already seen in the trailers. For instance, we get to see Austin Abrams rummaging through drawers and closets looking for bullets for a shotgun he pilfered (Heavy Ammo Shotgun Shells), running into padlocks that impede his progress, and, of course, a typewriter sitting in what appears to be a safe room.

More recently, we got a promotional poster for the film with a delivery slip detailing an organ transplant to Umbrella Corp, confirming that the shadowy biotech group is involved in Cregger’s movie. A teaser on social media also showed off a few first-person action sequences that hearken back to Resident Evil 7 and 8.

Cregger previously spoke on fans’ reactions to the movie with IGN at San Diego Comic-Con, where he admitted that he “took liberties” with his adaptation and explained why he chose not to make one-to-one adaptations of existing games in the series.

“The games are so well executed, and to me, Leon and Claire and these characters, they exist so perfectly in the games that anyone I cast and any difference that I do with them would be, probably, to the detriment of what I was trying to do,” he told us.

Resident Evil releases in theaters on September 18, 2026.

items.title: The Witcher 4, Cyberpunk 2077 Developer CD Projekt Red Ramps Up Hiring on 'Project Hadar'
items.description: The Witcher and Cyberpunk developer CD Projekt Red is staffing up for its unannounced 'Project Hadar', as that team is currently over 30 people strong with plans "to hire more, up to 50 developers by the end of this year," CD Projekt Red vice president of investor relations Karolina Gnas said on the company latest earnings call on Wednesday.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
The Witcher and Cyberpunk developer CD Projekt Red is staffing up for its unannounced 'Project Hadar', as that team is currently over 30 people strong with plans "to hire more, up to 50 developers by the end of this year," CD Projekt Red vice president of investor relations Karolina Gnas said on the company latest earnings call on Wednesday. The Project Hadar news was first reported by GamesRadar.

"Right now, the team is mostly focused on testing different approaches, ideas, and, you know, prototyping some gameplay element, and this is it," Gnas added. "Hadar is still in the concept phase." CDPR also confirmed that the remake of The Witcher 1 is on hold in favor of putting more resources into The Witcher 4, which the studio is targeting for a 2028 release, as well as the just-announced decade-later Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past.

But what is Project Hadar? It's tough to guess at this point, as The Witcher is a third-person fantasy RPG, while Cyberpunk is a first-person RPG shooter. Hadar being an RPG of some caliber is the only reasonably safe bet at this point.

Regardless, CDPR is nothing if not busy, with The Witcher 3 Remastered due out this month (and thankfully, existing owners get upgraded free and, yes, your old save files will work), plus The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past, The Witcher 4, a Cyberpunk sequel, the aforementioned Witcher 1 remake, and Project Hadar all in development.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

items.title: Over 600 Unused Voice Lines From Resident Evil 4 Leak Online, Showing That Capcom Intended to Connect the Game to Village
items.description: Over 30 minutes’ worth of unused voice lines from Resident Evil 4 Remake have surfaced online, one of which proves that Capcom wanted to make a connection to Village.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Ovee 30 minutes’ worth of unused voice lines from Resident Evil 4 Remake have surfaced online, one of which proves that Capcom wanted to make a connection to Village.

This leak comes from a notable community modder named Keff0, who uncovered both audio and subtitles for a whopping 671 lines on the game’s PlayStation 5 launch disc. These lines aren’t on the PC version of the game, and they’re fully recorded, featuring dialogue from Leon, Luis, Ashley, and the Merchant.

One of the Merchant’s unused lines is standing out to viewers, as he mentions a character that wasn’t even a blink in the RE Team’s mind when the game was first made back in the mid-2000s.

“Ah, I see you’re no stranger to villages. The Duke? Lad shows promise,” the Merchant says.

Resident Evil fans will make the connection to the series’ eighth game, Village, which features another merchant character who simply calls himself ‘The Duke.’ Funny enough, The Duke also references the Resident Evil 4 merchant as players browse through his wares, saying, “‘What’re ya buyin’?’ Haha, just something an old friend of mine used to say.”

Capcom’s decision to cut The Merchant’s line from RE4 Remake is a bit saddening, as it would have further cemented the relationship between these characters and added a bit more continuity to the timeline, if retroactively. However, this insertion of a modern-day Resident Evil character in the series’ single-most beloved game could have rubbed some players the wrong way, though we’ll never know for certain why Capcom chose to leave this particular dialogue out of the final product.

😮Over 600 cut voice lines have been found in Resident Evil 4 Remake.

Modder Keff0, who previously restored the game’s cut Chapter 0 and made it playable, has now uncovered 671 finished voice lines that were cut from Resident Evil 4 Remake.

🔎All of the lines can be found on… pic.twitter.com/obSogcJG6t

— RENEWS (@RENews_X) September 1, 2026

This wasn’t the only interesting find from the RE4 Remake; Keff0 also uncovered unused animations for the Merchant’s death, meaning that originally, players would have been able kill him. His shop was even supposed to close after he died, and save data found by Keff0 shows that he’d be gone for the rest of the game. This would have made it more similar to the original, but it seems like the team at Capcom thought that’d be too counterintuitive to this modern rework of the title.

Like many AAA games, there’s a swath of unused lines, scenes, art, enemies, characters, and other assets in recent Resident Evil titles that don’t make it to the final cut; earlier this year, Leon’s voice actor revealed that his favorite line in Resident Evil Requiem was ultimately axed by Capcom — and it’s a shame, because it was hilarious.

Luckily, there’s much more to come, with Code Veronica getting a remake in 2027 and a live-action Resident Evil movie directed by Zach Cregger set to hit theaters this month.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: The Witcher Remake Is on Hold Until The Witcher 4's Development Progresses, Confirms CD Projekt Red
items.description: The remake of The Witcher is currently on hold while the team focuses on The Witcher 4 and The Witcher 3's new expansion, according to CD Projekt Red.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The remake of The Witcher is currently on hold while the team focuses on The Witcher 4 and The Witcher 3's new expansion, according to CD Projekt Red.

Developer Fool's Theory is helping out on The Witcher 4 and developing The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion, but it is also attached to remake the first Witcher game. Unfortunately, that remake is on the hold for the time being. The studio confirmed this in a statement to GameSpot, noting that part of the hold up is due to the fact that the remake is being built on the back of The Witcher 4. As a result, the development team working on the remake will have to wait until The Witcher 4 gets further into development so that the remake can utilize all of the assets and tools created for the next installment.

“Fool’s Theory team is focused mainly on the development of Witcher 3: Songs of the Past, while a relatively small part of their team is supporting the development of The Witcher 4," said a CDPR rep. "As we have previously announced, the development on The Witcher Remake has been temporarily integrated with The Witcher 4 due to production process dependencies. As The Witcher Remake will be built on the foundation laid by The Witcher 4, we need to have the necessary assets, tools, and pipelines ready for efficient development.”

All in all, it doesn't sound like there's any reason to be concerned about whether The Witcher remake will see the light of day. Fool's Theory appears to be working on The Witcher 4 specifically so it can get familiar with the new tools and processes before continuing development on the remake. The Witcher remake was announced in 2022, and the team has openly talked about how it will be an open-world game that will remove or remake parts of the original that they feel are outdated or bad.

Ultimately, it sounds like we shouldn't expect The Witcher remake before 2028. CD Projekt Red has stated The Witcher 4 is currently slated to arrive in 2028, and it plans to complete a trilogy within six years of The Witcher 4's debut. It seems like the remake of The Witcher could come between The Witcher 4 and 5 to help keep fans busy.

CD Projekt Red is also developing a plethora of other projects, including a new IP, currently codenamed Project Hadar. Not much is known about the title, but CDPR confirmed today that it is ramping up hiring on the project while prototyping the game.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

Doug Cockle / The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt

"With voice actors, particularly with voice actors who do main character roles, it is a reality that people are ripping our voices off. That's happening. It's happened to me on multiple occasions. I can't even police it because I would spend all my time policing this stupid stuff. Every time somebody does that, they're effectively robbing me of income, and not just me, any other voice actor who they do it with. We're all watching our voices get used in ways that we would rather they weren't. Somebody could use AI to produce something racist using Geralt's voice, using my voice, or just something against anything that most normal people think is good. That's where the AI gets dangerous. Fake news, false news, false opinions. We're seeing it with politicians now. People are putting things out there. So AI is not the problem. It's the people using AI." Speaking to IGN.

items.title: TimTheTatman Turned Down Six-Figure Deal to Stream Arc Raiders Because He Hates It So Much
items.description: TimTheTatman has revealed that he turned down an eye-watering amount of money for a sponsored Arc Raiders stream.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
TimTheTatman has revealed that he turned down an eye-watering amount of money for a sponsored Arc Raiders stream.

The streamer was speaking candidly to his audience during a September 2 broadcast when he revealed that he'd turned down a six-figure deal to play Arc Raiders on stream for four hours. While the exact dollar amount is unknown, hundreds of thousands of dollars to play a game for an afternoon is an absolutely baffling amount of money. TimTheTatman stated that he had such an unpleasant experience with the game that even a jaw-dropping amount of cash couldn't bring him back.

"For me, the game frustrated me so much, I got frustrated so much with that game that I don't want to play it ever again," he said. "Even to a point where six figures didn't get me back on it."

TimTheTatman explains why he turned down a 6 figure ad deal to stream Arc Raiders for 4 hours.

“For me that game frustrated me so much that I never want to play it again. To a point where six figures couldn't get me back on it." pic.twitter.com/Ws8qyO6ye2

— ModernWarzone (@ModernWarzone) September 2, 2026

He joked that a seven-figure deal would be enough to make him get over his frustrations and play the game, but ultimately, it's not an experience he wants to revisit. Arc Raiders was one of the biggest games of 2025, but it has gradually declined over the last year. The game launched in a hyper-competitive window alongside the likes of Battlefield 6 and Call of Duty: Black Ops 7, but managed to capture a strong, supportive fan base at launch.

The game peaked with 465,000 concurrents on Steam in December 2025, two months after release, but things began to decline shortly after this. Arc Raiders players began to complain about a lack of meaningful new content and updates, causing players to lose interest. Eventually, Embark Studios confirmed that Arc Raiders would only get two major updates a year going forward and unfortunately, the studio just recently delayed future expeditions until 2027.

Naturally, some fans just aren't happy with the state of Arc Raiders. That lack of interest seems to be rubbing off on content creators who can't even muster some fake enthusiasm for a paycheck, it seems.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Ikea Is Coming to The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim and Fans Are All Saying the Same Thing
items.description: Ikea is partnering up with Skyrim in an unexpected collaboration that has fans making the same joke about The Elder Scrolls 6.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Ikea is partnering up with Skyrim in an unexpected collaboration that has fans making the same joke about The Elder Scrolls 6.

On September 2, the official Ikea accounts for Ireland and the United Kingdom posted a promotional video on Instagram, showing a mountain of familiar Skyrim memorabilia haphazardly tossed onto a snowy mountainside… alongside some comparatively modern-looking pieces.

For instance, a rune-inscribed Allen wrench is stuffed amongst the frozen Nord helmets, pots, swords, books, and wheels of cheese, while a white Kallax 4x2 shelf sits on top of the pile.

A date is then shown: September 9, 2026, along with the message, “Coming to the Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.” The post’s caption says much the same thing: “A Creation coming to The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.”

Thus far, it’s unclear exactly what this collaboration entails. Does this mean that the Kallax shelf will be available for players to decorate their homes with? Will they be able to use the magic Allen wrench as a weapon? (That would be hilarious.) Or is furniture from the game coming to IKEA?

items.title: Kat Dennings Recalls Her Six-Hour Mad Max: Fury Road Audition With 'Wonderful Person' Tom Hardy
items.description: Kat Dennings shared the heartwarming details of her Mad Max: Fury Road audition with Tom Hardy, revealing how a grueling screen test took a sweet turn in the end.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
2 Broke Girls and WandaVision actress Kat Dennings took to social media to recall her experience auditioning opposite Tom Hardy for 2015's Mad Max: Fury Road. Although Dennings at one point likens the audition to being like “an acting class if it was [on] the worst day of your life,” her story ultimately takes a surprisingly sweet and funny turn.

Dennings explained on TikTok how her screen test – she doesn’t specify which role she was up for but presumably it was for one of Immortan Joe’s Brides – took an epic six hours. It was a chemistry read between her and Hardy, who, of course, went on to win the title role of "Mad Max" Rockatansky.

Dennings, who still lived at home with her parents at the time, said director George Miller didn’t do much talking during the audition, with a person she believes was an acting coach leading the process instead.

@katdenningsss

With a twist at the end

♬ Quirky Suspenseful Indie-Comedy(1115050) - Kenji Ueda

“The dialogue was a couple of pages, and kind of vague. And basically, what happened was, an acting class, if it was, um, the worst day of your life. At one point, they had us switch roles. They had the camera and had us like running around the corner,” Dennings said.

“The worst part of it, I do believe, was when the acting coach told us to say the lines without saying the lines, encouraging us to just make noises instead of the lines. I was dying. I mean, Tom Hardy, he really took to this exercise. Like, he was able to be extremely free and come up with very creative ways of doing these lines.”

Dennings said “the best part of the story” is its ending and she’s absolutely right.

After the audition was finally over after six grueling hours, Dennings – who didn’t have a car – planned to go down the corner to call for a ride, but Hardy then offered to give her a lift.

“He drove me home. He was so lovely. We get to my house, which was my parents' house, because I still lived at home with my parents. And he came inside and he met my mom, and he was like, oh, what a nice house. She was like, oh, come on in. And I was like, all right, Tom, well, this is a very special day. Uh, I hope, uh, you move further in this experience because I know that I'm not going to. I went back to the converted garage where I lived, put my pajamas on, took a nap. A few hours later, I go back into the main house, and Tom Hardy is still there. Having tea with my mother, and just chatting it up. So... I can't say enough about Tom Hardy. I will be a fan of his for life. I think he's a wonderful person, and my mom still talks about him.”

While Dennings didn’t land a role in Mad Max: Fury Road, she did join the MCU as Darcy Lewis in the Thor films.

Hardy, you may have heard, just dropped a rap album he collaborated on with Czarface where, under the alias Frankie Pulitzer, he raps about everything from Willem Dafoe’s Green Goblin to Kathy Bates.

items.title: Sony Is Making 59% More Revenue Per PlayStation User Since PS4 Generation, Says Analyst
items.description: Sony is making 59% more money per active PlayStation user now than they were during the PS4 era, according to new data compiled by Niko Partners Director of Research and Insights Daniel Ahmad, who covers the video game market with a focus on the Asia and MENA markets. It translates to $230 more spent by the average active PlayStation user now than in 2018.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Sony is making 59% more money per active PlayStation user now than they were during the PS4 era, according to new data compiled by Niko Partners Director of Research and Insights Daniel Ahmad, who covers the video game market with a focus on the Asia and MENA markets. It translates to $230 more spent by the average active PlayStation user now than in 2018.

Responding to a new interview with Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki duscussing why the company isn't as aggressive in marketing the PS5 these days, Ahmad took to X to post, "I did the math on this and average annual revenue per PlayStation active user has grown from 23,580 Yen in FY2018 to 37,485 Yen in FY2025, which is around $230. [It's] an increase of 59% over that period. Although growth was flat over the past year or two."

For more detail and context, he added, "FY19 includes through to March 2020, with Covid leading to a boost in active users. Main drivers here are the transition to higher PS+ tiers, higher spending on game software and DLC / MTX, higher prices for hardware, etc." In short, Ahmad seems to suggest that Sony doesn't need to spend as much money to aggressively market the PS5, in the face of its and every console's rising prices, because it's making more money off of the users it already has.

Sony remains under fire from many gamers who are unsatisfied with the company's new physical games policy, which will see the company stop offering disc-based copies of games in January of 2028. Microsoft, meanwhile, is offering its Xbox players the chance to digitize their disc-based Xbox games as its next-gen Project Helix console/PC hybrid device approaches.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

items.title: A Playable Build of an Unreleased Scream Game Has Surfaced Thanks to the Steam Leak
items.description: An unreleased Scream game has found its way online thanks to the recent Steam leak.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
An unreleased Scream game has found its way online thanks to the recent Steam leak.

Last week, Steam was hit with a massive leak that saw tons of files and builds from the years 2003–2013 dumped online. It's been an interesting treasure trove for those who like gaming history, but one of the most unexpected things to come out of the incident is a playable build for a licensed Scream game that was never announced or released.

Kotaku spotted X / Twitter user roly poly reaper talking about the game and sharing never-before-seen gameplay.

update: we got multiplayer to work using goldberg emu + radmin VPN. heres footage of it running in the final build of the game pic.twitter.com/CpWOF9Y7RP

— roly poly reaper (@fellarobux) August 31, 2026

Interestingly enough, the game appears to be very similar to the likes of Dead by Daylight. One player would fill the shoes of Ghostface and track down ordinary players who are trying to collect evidence against the killer. The game was in the works from a developer known as Fatshark and would've predated Dead by Daylight and the Friday the 13th games, meaning it was a bit ahead of its time.

It's unclear exactly when this was developed, but it wouldn't be surprising if this took place around the time of Scream 4 in 2011. The franchise had been on ice for a decade prior to that film, so it would make sense if the rights owners were trying to generate some brand synergy. While we'll never get to play the finished version of this Scream game, some of the fans digging through the files were able to get multiplayer working.

It's an interesting relic from the past and one that would probably make more sense these days, should Paramount Games be interested in taking another crack at things. Dead by Daylight is still a huge title, and later this week, Halloween: The Game will release for early access owners. Whether that one sticks the landing remains to be seen, but previews have been pretty positive so far.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: 77-Year-Old Volunteer Teacher Arrested After Striking Young Student in Altercation Over Pokemon Cards
items.description: A 77-year-old volunteer teacher was arrested after reportedly striking a young student in a dispute over Pokémon cards.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
A 77-year-old volunteer teacher was arrested after reportedly striking a young student in a dispute over Pokémon cards.

A statement posted to the Dothan Police Department website by Chief William E. Benny describes the shocking incident, which took place on August 31, 2026.

That day, Dothan Police school resource officers responded to reports of an altercation between a student under the age of 10 and a volunteer teacher at the Jerry Lee Faine Elementary School in Dothan, Alabama.

The teacher, 77-year-old Oscar Truitt Jr., reportedly got into a feud with the student over Pokémon cards. Video footage taken from surveillance cameras on site showed Truitt “striking the child several times.” The volunteer teacher was charged with Harassment and booked into the Dothan City Jail after the incident.

“The safety of students is the top priority of the Dothan Police Department’s role in Dothan City Schools,” the statement reads.

At the time of writing, no other information about the altercation has been publicly revealed, leaving it unclear which Pokémon cards were involved in the dispute and whether or not the student is physically okay.

This is far from the first time someone’s been charged with a crime over Pokémon cards; we’ve covered a slew of similar stories over the last few years, with the most recent centering on a collector who organized his own ‘sting’ operation to catch thieves who gave him phony currency and ran off with three PSA Grade 10 cards worth $4,000 during a transaction gone wrong.

And in May, a Florida man was arrested and charged with burglary and theft of goods totalling more than $10,000 after reportedly breaking into a card shop using a chainsaw in West Palm Beach.

The fever around Pokémon cards has gotten so intense that Pokémon stores across Japan are taking measures to prevent scalping, with some implementing facial recognition software to discourage theft, while others are asking customers to pass a quiz in order to save card packs for real fans.

items.title: Andrew Garfield Historical Drama The Uprising Gets a Fortnite Crossover
items.description: Fortnite is officially crossing over with Andrew Garfield’s medieval rebellion film The Uprising, including historical melee weapons and film-inspired cinematic endings unique to each outcome.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
Nothing screams Fortnite like the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, am I right?

Focus Features announced Wednesday that the new movie The Uprising, starring Andrew Garfield, is now available to play as a custom experience on Fortnite ahead of the Paul Greengrass-directed film’s theatrical release on September 10.

Even for Fortnite – which has a long history of pop cultural collaborations including Star Wars, Marvel, DC, LEGO, The Witcher, Godzilla and Kong, Stranger Things, John Wick, and Back to the Future – The Uprising is a curious film to see on this platform.

The period drama – which may or may not (still) be a Robin Hood origin movie – chronicles the Peasants’ Revolt of 1381, which was led by historical figures Wat Tyler (played by Shogun’s Cosmo Jarvis) and John Ball (played by Jamie Bell). Andrew Garfield’s lead character, Ploughman, is meant to represent the Everyman peasant pushed by misfortune into taking up arms against the crown.

According to the official announcement, “the free Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN) experience, developed by Sawhorse Productions and published by Genesis Studios, immerses players in the heart of the legendary uprising, bringing the film's world to life through a large-scale multiplayer battle inspired by the events and visual landscape of The Uprising.”

“Set in 1380s England, the custom 5v5 payload-escort experience pits Rebels against Kingsmen in a battle for London’s gates. Rebel forces must push a battering-ram through four escalating map phases, advancing from muddy farmland to the fortified city walls, while Kingsmen fight to stop their advance before time expires. Players wield era-inspired melee weapons and bows, earn in-match currency and strategically upgrade their health, speed, and damage throughout the fight.”

Focus says The Uprising experience “culminates in film-inspired cinematic endings unique to each outcome, allowing players to uncover another layer of The Uprising’s story whether they emerge victorious as Rebels or successfully defend the kingdom as Kingsmen.”

Do you plan on playing The Uprising in Fortnite? Let us know in the comments.

For more Fortnite coverage, read the latest on that viral gaming chair toilet in “used” condition, the roster of iconic video game characters set to appear in the upcoming Overdrive season, and the new Star Wars skin that you need to visit Disneyland to unlock.

items.title: Eren Yeager's English Voice Actor Literally Dislocated His Jaw to Pull Off One of Attack on Titan's Most Iconic Moments
items.description: Bryce Papenbrook, the English voice actor for Eren Yeager, claimed that he literally dislocated his jaw in order to realistically sell one of the most intense moments in Attack on Titan.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Bryce Papenbrook, the English voice actor for Eren Yeager, claimed that he literally dislocated his jaw in order to realistically sell one of the most intense moments in Attack on Titan.

Warning: Spoilers for Attack on Titan follow!

Season 2 of Attack on Titan contains one of the most iconic scenes in the entire show. In this scene, Eren speaks with fellow Scouting Legion recruits Reiner and Bertholdt after a long, arduous series of events. This particular moment reveals a major betrayal from the two soldiers, who admit that they are the Titan-shifters who broke through the wall all those years ago, resulting in untold deaths and the tragic demise of Eren’s mother.

If you’re a sub-only viewer, you’ve been familiarized with Yuki Kaji’s masterful take on the line, “You damn traitors!” but Bryce Papenbrook is also a heavy-hitter here. In fact, he was so dedicated to portraying Eren’s sadness at Reiner and Bertholdt’s betrayal that he literally inflicted physical pain upon himself by dislocating his jaw.

Papenbrook revealed this startling information during a panel at Anime NYC this August, drawing confusion from fellow panelist and voice actor Cristina Vee.

“In that moment, he’s more unhinged than ever before. So I literally unhinged my jaw before that take, because I wanted that pain to come through,” he explained.

“What do you mean — physically unhinged? On purpose?” Vee asked, clearly stunned.

“Yeah,” Papenbrook answered. “Like, physically pushing my jaw out of place to force pain into the feeling because of how Eren was feeling in that moment. For Eren, I really wanted to feel what he was feeling, so in Season 1, when he bites his hand, I bit my hand so hard I left bruises.”

Bryce Papenbrook, 'ATTACK ON TITAN' English voice actor for Eren Yeager, reveals he dislocated his jaw to record Eren's voice lines during the big Season 2 reveal

"I literally unhinged my jaw before that take, because I wanted that pain to come through" pic.twitter.com/dVCcx3BiHw

— Anime Updates (@animeupdates) September 2, 2026

Fans were left equal parts shocked and impressed by Papenbrook’s dedication to the job, with one writing on X, “Dub hate is so insanely forced, ‘cause how do people see this and call it bad?”

items.title: YouTuber Claims Rockstar Confirmed Fans Measured Oxygen Levels Around Its Campus in Anticipation for a New Trailer
items.description: Italian YouTuber Mike ShowSha got to visit Rockstar ahead of the company’s big GTA 6 Netflix showcase, where developers told him that overeager fans were literally measuring the oxygen levels around their campus in anticipation for a new trailer.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Italian YouTuber Mike ShowSha got to visit Rockstar ahead of the company’s big GTA 6 Netflix showcase, where developers told him that overeager fans were literally measuring the oxygen levels around their campus in anticipation for a new trailer.

Back in June, a GTA superfan went viral for supposedly measuring oxygen levels around the Rockstar North campus. Their thinking was that, if these levels increased, more staff were on site, meaning that the team was working especially hard or preparing for a big announcement.

This same fan had set up acoustic audio equipment outside the campus and even camped outside the area, monitoring traffic from incoming and outgoing employees in a desperate attempt to gauge the status of the game’s development process.

Update: He started monitoring oxygen around Rockstar North, and he believes Trailer 3 is coming soon after noticing that oxygen levels dropped to around 20.3% and 20.04% after 5 PM, suggesting increased oxygen consumption in the area after normal working hours.

(Source:… https://t.co/nG5kOSTgkh pic.twitter.com/9XiN31cNLU

— GTA 6 Countdown ⏳ (@GTAVI_Countdown) June 7, 2026

YouTuber Mike ShowSha was one of the lucky creators who got invited to Rockstar’s offices to see the game up close and personal before its extended look went live on Netflix — and he claims that employees confirmed this superfan really did measure the oxygen levels at their workplace.

“Guys, I’ve been told some weird things,” the YouTuber said in an August 28 video, via machine translation. “Like, there are people who measure oxygen levels — I don’t know how they do it, but they told me this at Rockstar, so I’d tend to believe them, because if there’s a sign that suggests there are more people inside the studios, it means development has increased, and therefore it’s about to happen. It's crazy.”

Responses to this anecdote have been equal parts hilarious and disturbed, with one joking on X, “No wonder they started the trailer with, ‘Yoo, Crackheads!’”

“That level of obsession over a trailer is wild,” another said.

“Bruh, who thinks like this?” another asked. “I mean, it's pretty smart, but think about what people would do if they really want something.”

Grand Theft Auto 6 finally launches on November 19, 2026, when it will officially put the ‘We got [XYZ] before GTA 6’ memes to rest. We got to see a good look at what we can expect from the extended Netflix showcase, as well as from our own visit to the Rockstar offices, where we learned 69 new details about the game — including the fact that you don’t have to actively engage with Jason and Lucia’s relationship mechanic if you don’t feel like it.

While hype for this game is at an all-time high, not everyone is enthusiastic about its likely record-breaking launch, with some spouses taking to social media to claim that those who play the game are effectively cheating, due to the relationship between Jason and Lucia. We don’t know what’s wilder — that, or a fan literally camping outside Rockstar’s campus to measure its oxygen levels.

items.title: Disney Was Working on Its Own Smash Bros.-Like Fighting Game, Confirms Ex-Concept Artist
items.description: Former Disney Interactive concept artist Ken Christiansen confirmed that Kingdom Hearts inspired a Smash Bros.-like crossover fighting game that never got off the ground.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Former Disney Interactive concept artist Ken Christiansen confirmed that Kingdom Hearts inspired a Smash Bros.-like crossover fighting game that never got off the ground.

In 2013, Christiansen posted a slew of artworks to his online portfolio, some of which showed rough sketches of various Disney characters facing off in battle. It sparked the idea that Disney had possibly toyed with a crossover fighting game — something that Christiansen has now confirmed.

Speaking with Time Extension in a September 1 interview, Christiansen opened up about the surprising way Kingdom Hearts helped bring the idea to life, though it ultimately never came to fruition. In fact, it was difficult for Kingdom Hearts to get approved in the first place, as Disney execs were hesitant to combine some of the brand’s most iconic properties.

"One of the reasons Kingdom Hearts was so difficult to get started was because Disney was so reluctant to have that possibility of crossing over The Lion King into The Little Mermaid world," he explained. "That was the main hangup for Disney America. They couldn't get over that. So, I think there was maybe just a little bit of butting of heads, but it all worked out in the end. All of the creatives, though — like me, the other artists, and the producers — we all thought it was the greatest idea in the world. Like, 'Yeah, let's cross over everything.'"

"Since Kingdom Hearts already kind of broke that mold, producers would say, 'Hey, what if we say they're action figures, and we kind of take the same conceit as Toy Story, but have them fight each other instead?' Then, we can have all these action figures of Disney characters from Tarzan, The Lion King, and Treasure Planet, and it can be this Smash Brothers kind of thing. The title of that concept was 'Disney's Action Figure Face Off."

Unfortunately, this game never came to be; Time Extension reports that the project only reached the prototype stage before Disney ditched the idea in favor of movie and TV tie-in games.

With this in mind, the concept art shared to Christiansen’s portfolio makes us even more wistful for this game that never happened. The artwork showed 1v1 battles between eight different characters: Captain Hook vs Beast, the Sheriff of Nottingham vs King Louie, Ursula vs John Silver, and the Queen of Hearts vs the Horned King. Some of these characters are seriously deep cuts (we’d never expect to see the Horned King in any major Disney offering these days, let alone the Sheriff of Nottingham), and it makes us wonder who’d get chosen if such a game were to actually get made in the modern day.

"Often, when we were pitching a game at Disney, what they wanted from us was these gigantic presentation boards with art all over it. So you would get these big, six- or eight-foot-long boards that were maybe four feet high, like one-inch-thick foam core, and then over it were all these pieces of artwork printed out with big logos. So it was a big visual impact kind of thing. This was all so that you could walk the executives through the game. This led to things that did come out, like Disney's Extreme Skate Adventure,” he continued.

"Over my four years at Disney, I worked on so many concepts that never happened," said Christiansen. "I think that if there was a movie or a TV show, I probably carried it through, like Treasure Planet, Atlantis, Peter Pan 2, or Kim Possible — those games got money — or Pixar stuff like Buzz Lightyear and Monsters, Inc. But there was so much discussion about, 'What do we do with all these properties that we have?' So there's a lot of concept stuff for things that made it out.”

Speaking of Disney and games, an extended gameplay trailer for Kingdom Hearts IV was shown at D23 this year, showing off the Land of the Dead from Coco and a closer look at the modern city of Quadratum. KHIV is expected to launch in late 2027, a release window that director Tetsuya Nomura says Square Enix is firmly set on.

items.title: Final Fantasy Maker Square Enix Denies Rumors That It's Going Private
items.description: Square Enix has spoken out to address rumors that it's going private.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Final Fantasy developer Square Enix has spoken out to address rumors that it's going private.

Japanese business magazine Sentaku recently reported that Square Enix was looking into going private, leading to a nearly 12% increase in the company's stock price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. But this is not the case, Square Enix has said, responding to the claim.

"The September issue of the monthly magazine Sentaku carried a report regarding the possibility of Square Enix Holdings Co., LTD. (the 'Company') going private. However, this information was not announced by the Company," Square Enix said in a statement. "No consideration is currently being given within the Company to taking the Company private."

The news comes amid wider consolidation across the gaming industry. EA was recently acquired by a Saudi Arabian investment group and taken private, which has led to concerns from both fans and EA employees about what its new owners will do. Will they continue to invest in single-player games from BioWare and leverage beloved IP like Dead Space, or will they go heavy on microtransactions and live-service games? It'll be a while before we can really see the effects of the acquisition and EA's decision to go private, but naturally, a report like this for Square Enix can lead to rampant speculation about the company's future.

Square Enix itself has made a lot of changes this decade, with arguably the biggest adjustment being when it off-loaded a lot of its western studios, such as Crystal Dynamics and Eidos Montreal, in 2022. These teams were acquired by Embracer Group, meaning Square Enix no longer has the rights to franchises like Tomb Raider and Deus Ex. The company has also undergone multiple rounds of layoffs over the last few years, but has managed to soldier on.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: 'We're Improvisation-Based': Avengers: Doomsday Directors Defend Shooting Film Without a Finished Script
items.description: Avengers: Doomsday directors Joe and Anthony Russo have defended their decision to film the upcoming Marvel blockbuster without a finished script, with further tweaks to the movie taking place on set during shooting.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Avengers: Doomsday directors Joe and Anthony Russo have defended their decision to film the upcoming Marvel blockbuster without a finished script, with further tweaks to the movie taking place on set during shooting.

While this isn't the first MCU movie to evolve during production, Doomsday is undoubtedly one of Marvel's most challenging projects to date, with a vast cast of characters to balance, sky-high expectation to meet, and a sense that the return of Chris Evans and Robert Downey Jr. is something of a 'break glass in case of emergency' moment after a series of middling previous movies.

Word that pieces of Doomsday's intricate puzzle are being made up on the fly has naturally sparked concern among some fans, something that the Russos themselves have now sought to address.

"We always view the script as a living organism," says Joe Russo said, as reported by the Associated Press. "We're improvisation-based, rehearsal-based directors. We like to see what the actors bring to the characters, and sometimes you don't get the actors until a few days or few weeks before you shoot them. And a lot of the time, that's when the magic happens."

With so many characters in the mix, there's some sense to seeing which groups or pairings of actors end up having the most chemistry on set, and there's no suggestion that the main plot beats of the movie aren't locked down ahead of time. Here, the Russos seem to be talking more about specific lines of dialogue or character moments that may arise organically on set.

Still, with just over three months to go until Avengers: Doomsday releases, the Russos are still tinkering with the movie. It's understood that further reshoots are now taking place with additional and returning cast members (Hawkeye actor Jeremy Renner has teased his involvement), tacked on to the production window that will soon begin for next year's Avengers: Secret Wars.

How will it all turn out? We don't have long until Doomsday itself on December 18 when the movie finally arrives in theaters.

items.title: New Harry Potter Trailer Teases Snape, Quidditch, and the Sorting Hat
items.description: The latest Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone trailer teases key moments including Professor Snape, Quidditch, the Sorting Hat, and Harry’s parents.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
HBO has released a new trailer for Harry Potter and The Philosopher’s Stone, the second teaser for the eight-episode season that will debut Christmas 2026 on HBO and available to stream on HBO Max.

The trailer shows highlights such as: first-year student Harry Potter (Dominic McLaughlin) wearing the Sorting Hat and being chosen for Gryffindor; the beginnings of the friendship between Harry, Hermione Granger (Arabella Stanton), and Ron Weasley (Alastair Stout); a Quidditch match; Ron getting his acceptance letter to Hogwarts and a better look at the Weasley family; potions professor Severus Snape (Paapa Essiedu) being unimpressed with Harry; Harry using the Cloak of Invisibility; the Mirror of Erised; the Troll in the bathroom; and various moments featuring John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall, and Nick Frost as Rubeus Hagrid.

There are also some quick shots of what appears to be a flashback to Harry’s parents Lily and James Potter running across a bridge, as well as what might be our first look at Lord Voldemort.

THE NEW HBO’s HARRY POTTER TRAILER IS HERE

Releasing this Christmas on HBO pic.twitter.com/OvCm0Lz4bL

— Wizarding World Direct (@WW_Direct) September 2, 2026

The cast of Harry Potter and The Philosopher’s Stone includes Rory Wilmot as Neville Longbottom, Lox Pratt as Draco Malfoy, Leo Earley as Seamus Finnigan, Elijah Oshin as Dean Thomas, Tristan Harland as Fred Weasley, Gabriel Harland as George Weasley, Ruari Spooner as Percy Weasley, Alessia Leoni as Parvati Patil, Sienna Moosah as Lavender Brown, Finn Stephens as Vincent Crabbe, William Nash as Gregory Goyle, Warwick Davis as Filius Flitwick and Sirine Saba as Pomona Sprout.

Additional cast includes Daniel Rigby as Vernon Dursley, Bel Powley as Petunia Dursley, Paul Whitehouse as Argus Filch, Johnny Flynn as Lucius Malfoy, Bertie Carvel as Cornelius Fudge, Luke Thallon as Quirinus Quirrell, Katherine Parkinson as Molly Weasley, Amos Kitson as Dudley Dursley, Gracie Cochrane as Ginny Weasley, Richard Durden as Cuthbert Binns, Louise Brealey as Rolanda Hooch, Bríd Brennan as Poppy Pomfrey, Leigh Gill as Griphook and Anton Lesser as Garrick Ollivander.

Based on J.K. Rowling’s beloved books, the series is written and executive produced by Francesca Gardine.

Season 2 of Harry Potter begins filming in the fall with Kit Harrington taking on the role of the Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher Gilderoy Lockhart (replacing Nicholas Hoult).

Back to Hogwarts celebrations kicked off on September 1, and there may still be more Potter announcements coming.

items.title: ‘It’s Not a Revolutionary Thing for an RPG to Have’ — Fable Explains the Very Obvious Reason as to Why Its Hero Design Has Changed
items.description: Fable's game director Ralph Fulton spoke to us at gamescom 2026 about character customization and confirms: Yes, it's in there.
items.author: Simon Cardy
items.content:
Character creators are no new thing when it comes to video games, especially RPGs. Fable is just one in a very long line of adventures allowing you to sculpt a hero in your image, but when it comes time to showcase a game ahead of time, decisions need to be made.

From its initial reveal onward, we’ve become accustomed to seeing multiple chosen hero appearances throughout trailers and gameplay videos, of all shapes, sizes, and genders. But that first female hero is who has become the poster child for Playground’s reboot, with some people deciding it would be a perfectly normal thing to do to complain about her not being conventionally “attractive” enough.

Well, at gamescom 2026, the Forza Horizon studio revealed a new extended look at quest gameplay taking place in Albion’s capital of Bowerstone, in which the player hero took the form of a woman we hadn’t seen before. A response to online backlash or just a simple example of the variations available when playing around with Fable’s character creator? I asked game director Ralph Fulton.

“Earlier this year, we obviously revealed that we have had some customization in our game,” Fulton explains. “It's not a revolutionary thing for an RPG to have, but nevertheless, there was some speculation that we didn't, and we were happy to reveal: Yes, we did.”

Since then, in the assets we've put out; our showcase trailer, the live gameplay video we put out in June and both of our assets here, we've been happy to start just cycling through some of the characters you can select and customize using that tool. The girl that you see in the theater demo that we're showing today is just another one of the characters that you can select and customize in the game. And you know what? People like her, I'm delighted.”

Fable will launch on February 23, 2027, and you’ll have the freedom to make your character look however you like. It really is that simple.

For more on the RPG, you can check out not one, but two previews from gamescom 2026, where I gave my impressions of the new quest gameplay, plus my thoughts on its combat having played it.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social.

items.title: How to Watch PlayStation’s September 2026 State of Play
items.description: Sony announced two State of Play streams for September 3. Here's how you can watch the announcements live.
items.author: Leanne Butkovic
items.content:
Should the plural of “State of Play” be States of Play or State of Plays? Either way, Sony is starting September with two back-to-back showcase streams — a State of Play and a State of Play Japan — on Thursday, September 3. These will be the second and third State of Play of the year following the one in early June, which gave us that bloody Wolverine opening (cool) and the first big look at God of War Laufey. In its August 31 blog post, Sony didn’t provide many specifics about what to expect outside of an “extended look” at Final Fantasy VII Revelation and the typical promise of "updates and announcements," but we have some ideas about what we'll see (more on that below).

IGN will be carrying the stream; here’s everything you need to know about how to watch, where to watch, and what you can expect from the double-header State of Play lineup.

When Does PlayStation’s September 2026 State of Play Start?

Sony will kick off the first State of Play on September 3 at 6am PT / 9am ET / 3pm CEST / 10pm JST. The company didn’t say how long that one will go (though they typically run for about 40 minutes), but the State of Play Japan, hosted by Yuki Kaji, will immediately follow. Both streams will be in English and Japanese (hosted in English with Japanese subtitles available for the first; hosted in Japanese and subtitled in English for the second).

We’ll be hosting a pre-show 15 minutes before the start of the first presentation at 5:45am PT / 8:45am ET / 2:45pm CEST / 9:45pm JST.

Once the Sony streams wrap, IGN will be live again for a Beyond post-show to discuss everything we just saw.

We’ll also be liveblogging these streams and covering everything that gets announced — stay tuned for all the news.

How to Watch the September 2026 PlayStation State of Play

IGN will be hosting State of Play streams right on IGN dot com, as well as all the classic social channels and our handy-dandy app. Here are all of those links:

  • IGN’s homepage
  • IGN’s YouTube channel
  • IGN's Twitch channel
  • IGN's Facebook
  • IGN’s Twitter
  • The IGN app (on iOS and Android)

What to Expect From the September 2026 PlayStation State of Play

A double stream! That’s fun. In its blog post, Sony teased the classic “updates and announcements from PlayStation Studios and our third-party partners” and will end on ”an extended look at the vast world of Final Fantasy VII Revelation.” (We also got a not-so-extended look at the game that highlighted the Weapons out of gamescom's Opening Night Live.)

What else? Well, maybe one last look at Marvel’s Wolverine before it comes out later this month, God of War Laufey, a Ghost of Yotei DLC, Kingdom Hearts 4, Control Resonant, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, Resident Evil: Veronica… Would it finally be time to get another look at Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet? It was noticeably absent from June's SoP and it did just wrap performance capture.

You can read more on all of our inklings on what we might see from the State of Play streams. Of course, expect plenty of surprises.

Sony’s been in hot water lately with its insistent commitment to ending physical games by 2028. You can surely expect the chat to be popping off with people having big feelings about it — that’s what happened during the Phantom Blade Zero stream in mid-August.

For more, check out what was revealed at last year’s September State of Play and this year’s Summer Games Fest back in June.

Leanne Butkovic (she/they) is the Editorial Programming Manager at IGN, where they've also written about TV, movies, and games.

items.title: After 10 Years, Pokémon Go Is Getting a Pokémon Anime Crossover Episode
items.description: The world of Pokémon Go will cross over into the Pokémon anime series, in an episode where the gang meet Professor Willow and spin a PokéStop.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
The world of Pokémon Go will cross over into the Pokémon anime series later this month, in an episode where the gang meet Professor Willow and spin a PokéStop.

Pokémon Go celebrated its 10th anniversary this summer, and the celebrations will continue this month as a landmark episode of the Pokémon Horizons series debuts in Japan on September 18, featuring a couple of very special guest stars.

Yes, Professor Willow himself will be making his anime debut, leaping over from his role assisting players in Pokémon Go. Coming along with him is Meltan, his partner Pokémon, and at least one PokéStop — the identifiers of real-world locations that Pokémon Go players spin in-game.

9月18日（金）18時55分から、『Pokémon GO』とアニポケのコラボエピソード放送が決定！
『Pokémon GO』内でも、テレビアニメコラボが開催されるよ。
コラボPVが解禁されたから、チェックしてね！https://t.co/VzJHnpeL7y #アニポケ #ポケモンGO pic.twitter.com/TWKMfTl5Wa

— ポケモン公式 (@Pokemon_cojp) September 2, 2026

In a trailer posted today by the official Japanese Pokémon social media account, above Captain Pikachu can be seen spinning the PokéStop, accurately recieving Pokéballs and berries as a reward. And in a further nod, a Kecleon is revealed to have been hiding in plain sight — a neat nod to how the chameleon-like creature can be caught in Pokémon Go.

Exactly how Professor Willow will cross paths with Roy, Liko, and the series' other characters remains to be seen, as Go's canonicity with the rest of the Pokémon franchise has always been left unclear. Indeed, Meltan and Melmetal, which debuted first in Pokémon Go, lack an official region of origin (such as Johto or Kanto), and are instead listed as being discovered in an "Unidentified" place.

Regardless, Pokémon Horizons and Go will also crossover together within Pokémon Go itself, with the episode's Charizard wearing goggles available to catch in Go, as well as a return for Captain Pikachu. All of that takes place between September 16 and 22, around the time the special episode airs first in Japan. In the U.S., fans can start watching Pokémon Horizons: Season 3 via Netflix, while in the U.K. the series debuts on BBC iPlayer.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social
